title: LinguaMark: Do Multimodal Models Speak Fairly? A Benchmark-Based Evaluation

bias_targets.methodology: Prompt-based evaluation using an LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini) to compare two model responses to visual question answering (VQA) prompts differing only by gender, classifying them as 'Biased' or 'Neutral' based on meaningful differences in tone, content, or assumptions.

Prompt-based evaluation using an LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini) to compare two model responses to VQA prompts differing only by race/ethnicity, classifying them as 'Biased' or 'Neutral' based on meaningful differences in tone, content, or assumptions.

Prompt-based evaluation using an LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini) to compare two model responses to VQA prompts differing only by age, classifying them as 'Biased' or 'Neutral' based on meaningful differences in tone, content, or assumptions.

Prompt-based evaluation using an LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini) to compare two model responses to VQA prompts differing only by occupation, classifying them as 'Biased' or 'Neutral' based on meaningful differences in tone, content, or assumptions.

Prompt-based evaluation using an LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini) to compare two model responses to VQA prompts differing only by the sports attribute, classifying them as 'Biased' or 'Neutral' based on meaningful differences in tone, content, or assumptions.

Evaluating and comparing model performance metrics (Bias, Answer Relevancy, and Faithfulness) in an open-ended VQA task across 11 diverse languages to measure disparities between high-resource languages (e.g., English) and low-resource languages (e.g., Tamil, Urdu).
